evals.prompt: I'm writing a blog post about how a token-bucket rate limiter works. Can you make me one interactive isometric illustration for it, the polished kind (like Linear's site), as a single HTML file I can just open? My blog has a white background. The bucket holds 20 tokens, refills 5 per second, and each request takes one token; requests get rejected when it's empty.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone HTML file, light theme, with one framed isometric figure of a real physical object that explains a token bucket (tokens refilling, requests taking tokens, rejection when empty), live readout with true numbers, calm eased motion, keyboard/pointer interaction. Every curved part (a hopper, a drum, a funnel) is smooth-shaded with no stepped tone blocks, every row of ticks, ribs or bolt dots ends on a real edge or fades out instead of stopping mid-surface, and nothing passes through anything; any pipe or chute is recorded and `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed` with zero on every failing line. It was checked with 4x close-ups of every joint, and every PNG was looked at.

evals.prompt: We need a figure for our Next.js docs explaining database connection pooling: a pool of 10 connections, requests borrow a connection and give it back, and when all 10 are busy new requests wait in a queue. Build it as a React component (TSX) we can drop into the app, and also give me a static HTML preview so I can look at it right now. Dark theme. It should look like a crafted physical object with fine details, not a boxes-and-arrows diagram.
evals.expected_output: A React TSX component (plus any geometry/CSS files) and a standalone HTML preview, dark theme, showing connection pooling as a real object with many small parts, live readout, painter's order correct, motion/interaction. Lines, hoses or cables that represent connections run along the structure in lanes and land on real ports, never through another part or across the subject's face; where two cross on screen the nearer is drawn on top. If the figure has tubes or round parts, their shapes are recorded with kit/audit.mjs and the preview's build reports zero audit problems. Curved parts show no tone staircase and no texture stops abruptly. 4x close-ups of the junctions were taken and read.

evals.prompt: make an isometric svg explaining how a CDN edge cache works (cache hit vs miss, TTL of 60s) for our landing page. dark, premium, lots of small detail. just give me the svg file, and a png preview if you can
evals.expected_output: A standalone dark SVG file (styles embedded) of a crafted isometric object explaining a CDN edge cache (hit vs miss, TTL 60 s), rich in small parts, monochrome with one accent, no floating labels. No line passes through a part, every crossing is in depth order, curved surfaces are smooth-shaded without a staircase, and every texture (vents, ticks, bolt circles) ends on an edge or fades. A PNG preview plus 4x close-ups were made and looked at.

evals.prompt: For a chemistry explainer, make an interactive isometric figure of a Bunsen burner on a lab bench, showing how opening the air collar turns the lazy yellow flame into a roaring blue cone. I want the flame to look real, so use a WebGL shader for it, but keep the crafted line-drawing look for the burner itself. One HTML file I can open, dark theme.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone dark HTML page built with the kit. The burner is SVG with many small parts made with kit/lathe.mjs: a weighted base, a barrel, a rotating air collar with real air holes, a jet and a ribbed gas inlet with a hose from kit/tube.mjs, on a bench plate, with an optional tripod and gauze. Every curved profile (base dome, barrel flare, inlet) is smooth-shaded with no tone staircase, from smooth knots or an analytic profile with smooth.slope; the inlet ribs and any bolt circle fade toward the limb (ribsOf/dotsOf with fade) instead of stopping. The hose leaves the inlet along its axis, lies on the bench without passing through the base, tripod or bench, and is gapped under any clamp or band; all shapes are recorded with kit/audit.mjs and `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed`, zero on every failing line. The flame is a WebGL shader on glLayer (glScript inlined), in a canvas between a back SVG (bench, base, everything the flame covers) and a front SVG (whatever passes in front of it, such as the near tripod leg or gauze). The canvas has pointer-events none and blends with screen and premultiplied output. The flame lives in world space: it is ray-marched along towardViewer() around the barrel axis, sized in world units, and its base registers with the barrel rim from the same numbers as the SVG. Its colour and shape follow the air-to-gas ratio from a small model continuously (a luminous yellow sooty flame turning into a blue inner cone and pale outer mantle) through eased envelopes, with no instant colour switch. Lighting and turning off are attack-and-decay envelopes built on the kit's burst and settle (inlined by glScript, not redeclared), with constant geometry passed through glLayer's fixed uniforms. No term is cut at a bound or at the canvas edge, and the output is tonemapped and dithered. The device ratio is capped at 1.5, the shader renders only while lit and onscreen, reduced motion shows one still flame, and the SVG reads without WebGL. The live readout (collar opening, air/gas ratio, flame temperature) comes from the model, with pointer and keyboard control and an idle tour. The figure was checked with drive.mjs contact sheets slowed with ["slow", 0.05] across lighting, a full collar sweep and turning off, plus 2x and 4x crops at the barrel rim and 4x close-ups of the hose, inlet and collar in both themes, a --no-webgl run showing the SVG burner alone, and a --reduced run.

evals.prompt: For an article on how espresso machines work, make an interactive isometric figure of a heat-exchanger espresso machine with the side panel off: boiler, heat-exchanger tube, group head, pump, steam wand, pressure gauge and all the pipework between them. Show water flowing through when you pull a shot. Lots of fine detail, it should hold up when people zoom in. Standalone HTML, light theme.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page built with the kit: a real espresso machine with its side panel off, its boiler, group head, gauge and fittings turned with kit/lathe.mjs and its pipework from kit/tube.mjs, with a live readout from a small model (boiler pressure, brew temperature, flow) and a calm pull-a-shot interaction. Every pipe is routed from real ports along the structure (leaving each port on its normal, running parallel to the boiler or round it at a fixed radius, crossing other lines only on straights and well apart in depth), never across the front of the boiler or group; it ends on a flange, union nut or fitting on a real port, never in the air. Nothing is sunk into anything: flanges sit flush or on saddle pads on the curved boiler, branches leave from ball tees, valves sit on straight runs, and every collar, clamp, band or valve gaps the pipe it wraps. Every item records its shape in A.recorder, A.settle sets the painter's keys, and `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed`, zero on every failing line, with no interlock hidden by a key bias. The boiler, group head dome and gauge are smooth-shaded with no tone staircase or scalloped bands (analytic profiles with smooth.slope or bandsOf for the boiler), seams sit under the outline, and every bolt circle, rib row or rule line ends on a real edge or fades out (dotsOf/ribsOf with fade, fadeLineSvg). Pipe stripes run onto their end caps with no hairline at chunk joints. The response shows that 4x close-ups of every junction (each tee, flange, union, valve, clamp and crossing) and every curved body were taken in both themes and read, and that the water-flow motion has no pop.

evals.prompt: Can you make a diagram of our CI/CD pipeline for the engineering handbook, in that crafted isometric style rather than a flat flowchart? A push starts checkout (20 s), then lint (45 s) and unit tests (3 min 10 s) run side by side, then the Docker build (2 min 30 s), integration tests (4 min), deploy to staging (1 min), a manual approval, and deploy to production (1 min 30 s). I want readers to see where the time goes, to toggle the build cache (it cuts the build to 40 s), and to see what happens when integration tests fail. Standalone HTML; the handbook has light and dark modes, so I need both.
evals.expected_output: Two standalone HTML pages from one build.mjs (`node build.mjs` and `node build.mjs --light`) in diagram mode: a crafted map of the pipeline, not an invented machine and not a flat flowchart. Before any geometry the response writes the mapping (stage to block, the push to an outside actor in another shape language, the approval gate to its own glyph, each dependency to a tube, stage time to block height and to a segment on a minutes ruler along the front edge, the lint and unit-test pair to two half lanes on the timeline bar) and the inventory, about nine nodes, a Figure. The main flow runs along +x with the camera at azimuth 55–60° and elevation 30–36°; lint and unit tests split across two rows with the shorter block (lint) in front and the rows far enough apart to see over. Every stage is named on its front (+y) face, unsquashed and in clear view, at least about 6.5 viewBox units at 1×, with long names fitted to their face (fitText), no socket or tube on a label's span and no block in front of another's label. Stages rest at `mid`; `lit` (1.25 px) means running now, so lint and unit tests are lit together, and waiting is not working: no stage is lit while the run waits for approval. After a successful run the critical path is outlined `hi` and lint, the shorter branch, stays `mid`. Connections are recorded tubes from socket to socket with ferrules, and direction is shown by packets (a `lit` trail and head dot drawn inside each tube chunk), never by arrowheads, leader lines or floating text. A pure model module (`model.mjs`) returns every stage interval and hop for a given cache and failure setting, and the heights, ruler, bar, lit states, packets, critical path, readout and caption all read from it: 12:30 of stage time to production without the cache and 10:40 with it, the approval wait kept off the clock, and a failing run that stops after integration tests (10:00, or 8:10 with the cache) with no packet reaching staging or production. The cache and the failure are keys and clicks on the build and integration blocks, named in the hint; the tour cycles them; reduced motion jumps to the result with the full bar and the critical path. `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed` with zero on every failing line, and `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on both pages. Every label was looked at at 4× at rest and while lit, the parallel pair and a failed run were frozen with drive.mjs `until` and `slow` and looked at, and the response says what doesn't read at 390 px.

evals.prompt: For our API docs I need an interactive figure that explains our permission check. Roles are granted on an org, on a project inside the org, or on a repo inside the project, and grants inherit downward. When someone deletes a branch, the API asks the policy service, which checks the repo's grants first, then the project's, then the org's, and stops at the first role that includes branch:delete; if none does, the request is denied with a 403. Each grants lookup takes about 2 ms, except the org's, which is cached at 0.3 ms. Readers should be able to move the grant between the three levels or remove it and watch the check walk up. Dark theme, one HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone dark HTML page in diagram mode (the idea is a hierarchy and a lookup order, not a mechanism), with its `--light` build made too for the checks. The response writes the mapping and inventory first, each visual property carrying one true quantity or none: the user an outside actor, the API and policy service as blocks, each level's grants a store, the hierarchy as groups (for example nested trays, the repo's standing on the project's and the project's on the org's, so containment and inheritance read from the nesting), every lookup a tube from the policy service to a socket or boss on a grants store, and lookup time as height or on a ruler. About seven nodes, a Figure. The walk up the hierarchy runs back into the scene, never forward, with rows far enough apart that nothing stands in front of a labelled face. Blocks are named on their front (+y) faces, unsquashed, at least about 6.5 viewBox units at 1×; round stores are named on their top faces; each tray is named on a corner no tube crosses, or in the legend; no socket covers a label. Nodes rest at `mid`; `lit` means working now, so the policy service and the store it is reading are lit during each lookup, the stores not yet read and those skipped after a match stay unlit, and the API is unlit while it waits. At rest the path to the matching grant is outlined `hi` (on a denial the whole walk, with the 403 travelling back). Direction is packets on the tubes, the answer travelling back on the same tube, with no arrowheads, leader lines or floating text. A pure model module (`model.mjs`) takes where the grant is (repo, project, org or none) and returns every lookup interval and hop, and the readout, lit states, packets, `hi` path and caption all read from it: one lookup and 2.0 ms of lookup time for a repo grant, two and 4.0 ms for a project grant, three and 4.3 ms for an org grant or a denial, plus whatever hop time the model adds. A key cycles the grant level and a click on a level's grants store moves the grant there, named in the hint; the tour cycles all four cases with rest on each result; reduced motion jumps to the result. `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed` with zero on every failing line, and `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on the dark page and the light build. Every label was looked at at 4× at rest and while lit, one frame per case was frozen with drive.mjs `until` and `slow` (a numeric test for the 0.3 ms org lookup, which is shorter than the poll interval), and the response says what doesn't read at 390 px.

evals.prompt: I'm writing an article on event-driven architecture and want an interactive isometric figure of our order flow. Checkout publishes an OrderPlaced event to a queue, and three consumers each read it on their own subscription: payments (120 ms per message), inventory (40 ms) and email (900 ms). Orders come in at about 5 a second, so I want people to see the email backlog grow while the other two keep up, and failed messages land in a dead-letter queue after 3 retries. Let readers change the arrival rate and make the email consumer start failing. Light theme, one HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone light HTML page, with the dark build made too for the checks, in diagram mode: the idea is relational (a publisher, a queue, three subscriptions and a dead-letter queue, and what matters is who takes what and how fast), so the response maps the structure instead of inventing a machine, or asks which mode the user wants. The mapping and inventory come first, each visual property carrying one true quantity or none: checkout as a block or outside actor, the queue and the dead-letter queue as stores, the consumers as blocks with one quantity in their height (for example messages a second each can take), each subscription's lag as a state detail or a bar on a scale with numbers on the plane of their ticks, and every relationship as one tube from socket to socket. About six or seven nodes, a Figure. The flow runs along +x; the three consumers split across rows with the shorter blocks in front, the dead-letter queue sits behind the email consumer, and the rows are far enough apart that every label stays in view. Blocks are named on their front (+y) faces, unsquashed, at least about 6.5 viewBox units at 1× and fitted to their face; the stores are named on their top faces; no socket or tube covers a label. Nodes rest at `mid`; `lit` means working now, so a consumer is lit only while it is processing a message, payments and inventory light briefly and go dark between messages while email stays lit at 5 a second, and the queue holding messages is not lit, since waiting is not working. Each message is a packet (a `lit` trail and head dot inside each tube chunk): checkout to the queue, then one per subscription to its consumer, a retry back on the same tube, and a dead letter on to the dead-letter queue after its third retry. No arrowheads, leader lines or floating text. A pure, deterministic model module (`model.mjs`) gives every arrival, delivery, attempt and dead letter for a rate and failure setting, and the heights, lag, packets, lit states, readout and caption all read from it: at 5 a second email can take 1.1 a second, so its lag grows by about 3.9 messages a second while payments (8.3 a second) and inventory (25 a second) stay near zero. The rate and the failure are keys and clicks on the checkout and email blocks, named in the hint; the tour cycles them; the live region announces settled changes, not every tick; reduced motion shows one settled frame from the model. `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed` with zero on every failing line, and `node scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0` on the light page and the dark build. Every label was looked at at 4× at rest and while lit, the growing backlog, a retry and a dead letter were frozen with drive.mjs `until` and `slow` (a numeric test for inventory's 40 ms of work, shorter than the poll interval), and the response says what doesn't read at 390 px.
